title: Deriving proper/open support under all-sheaf finite cohomological dimension
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $p:V\to T$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and set $U=V\times_TW$, with projections $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $r:U\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the uncompleted unbounded derived operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Assume $p$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and assume an integer $d\geq0$ satisfies $R^qp_*F=0$ for every pro-etale $A$-module sheaf $F$ on $V$ and $q>d$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\gamma:i_!r_*\xrightarrow{\sim}p_*k_!$ for the specified sheaf comparison [lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison], and use exact extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero, lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. For $M\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, choose a K-injective representative $J$ with injective terms [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] and a K-injective resolution $k_!J\to I$. The map represented by
$$i_!r_*J\xrightarrow{\gamma_J}p_*k_!J\longrightarrow p_*I$$
defines an isomorphism $\Gamma_M:i_!Rr_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*k_!M$, independent of the choices and natural in $M$. With the canonical restriction isomorphism $\lambda$ of [lem-exc-proetale-derived-open-restriction], its specified normalization under $i_!\dashv i^*$ [prop-exc-open-adjoint] is
$$\lambda_M\circ i^*\Gamma_M=1_{Rr_*M},\qquad \Gamma_M=\varepsilon_i\circ i_!(\lambda_M^{-1}).$$
No quasi-compactness of $i$ or boundedness or etale-origin condition on $M$ is assumed.

proof.text: The already proved source-library full-faithfulness instances for open extension, transported through the intrinsic coefficient equivalences, make the sheaf open unit invertible. Apply exact termwise derived descent to this unit: j.mapDerivedCategory composed with t.mapDerivedCategory is isomorphic to the identity. The existing derived open adjunction is therefore fully faithful on the left (Adjunction.fullyFaithfulLOfCompIsoId). This establishes the essential-image criterion for its counit without any choice of a new adjunction.

Use the Grothendieck module-sheaf theorem and the source-library functorial degreewise-injective K-injective replacement. For M choose a complex preimage K under Q and let J be its replacement; localization inverts K to J and gives M isomorphic to QJ. For F=p_*, convert hcd to classical rightDerived vanishing using F.isZero_rightDerived_of_isZero_homology. The same conversion applied to Cartesian open injective acyclicity proves every term of k_!J is F-right-acyclic. Left exactness of the sectionwise direct image is the already proved proEtaleConstantModuleDirectImage_additive_leftExact theorem.

Apply the already proved source-library specialization of lem-kun-finite-cd-acyclic-complex, F.isIso_rightDerivedFunctorUnit_app_of_rightAcyclic, to k_!J. The quotientCompQhIso comparisons identify Rp_*(Q(k_!J)) with Q(p_*k_!J). Apply the specified sheaf isomorphism gamma degreewise and localize, giving Q(p_*k_!J) isomorphic to i_!Q(r_*J). Exact descent identifies k_!M with Q(k_!J). Compose these isomorphisms to obtain eY: Rp_*k_!M isomorphic to i_!Q(r_*J). Only an object-level essential-image witness is needed here; it is not substituted for the specified comparison morphism.

By full faithfulness from Step 1, the counit at every object isomorphic to an i_!-image is invertible (Adjunction.isIso_counit_app_of_iso applied to eY). The derived restriction theorem says that the specified lambda inverse is invertible. By its existing definition, the component of the canonical proper/open comparison is i_! of that lambda inverse followed by this counit. Both factors are isomorphisms. NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app gives invertibility of the specified natural transformation, without needing to identify an independently constructed map with it.

The same existing definition identifies each comparison component with homEquiv.symm of lambda inverse. Applying homEquiv and its apply_symm_apply identity gives the unit/restriction normalization. Expanding the inverse adjunction formula gives the displayed counit normalization by reflexivity. All constructions are in the existing ordinary unbounded categories; no boundedness, completion, quasi-compactness of the open, or etale-origin assumption was added.
